# Statistical plots

seaborn, plotnine (the grammar of graphics of ggplot2 in Python), pandas and
statsmodels draw with matplotlib: the plots are shown below the chunks (and in
the rendered document). Needs seaborn, plotnine and statsmodels (*Python
Packages*). The data set penguins is part of seaborn (downloaded once).

```{python setup}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
try:
    penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins").dropna()
except Exception:
    # Offline: similar data
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    species = np.repeat(["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"], 110)
    bill = np.concatenate([rng.normal(m, 2.5, 110) for m in (38.8, 48.8, 47.5)])
    flipper = np.concatenate([rng.normal(m, 6.5, 110) for m in (190, 196, 217)])
    mass = np.concatenate([rng.normal(m, 450, 110) for m in (3700, 3730, 5080)])
    penguins = pd.DataFrame({"species": species, "bill_length_mm": bill, "flipper_length_mm": flipper,
                             "body_mass_g": mass, "sex": np.tile(["Male", "Female"], 165)})
penguins.groupby("species")[["bill_length_mm", "flipper_length_mm", "body_mass_g"]].mean().round(1)
```

## seaborn

```{python}
sns.pairplot(penguins, hue="species", vars=["bill_length_mm", "flipper_length_mm", "body_mass_g"],
             height=2.2, plot_kws={"s": 18})
```

```{python}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
sns.violinplot(data=penguins, x="species", y="body_mass_g", hue="sex", split=True, ax=axes[0])
axes[0].set_title("Body mass")
sns.regplot(data=penguins, x="flipper_length_mm", y="body_mass_g", scatter_kws={"s": 12}, ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title("Body mass ~ flipper length")
fig.tight_layout()
```

```{python}
corr = penguins.select_dtypes("number").corr()
sns.heatmap(corr, annot=True, fmt=".2f", cmap="vlag", vmin=-1, vmax=1, square=True)
plt.title("Correlations")
plt.show()
```

## plotnine (grammar of graphics)

A plotnine plot is drawn with `p.draw()` (or `print(p)` / `p.show()`).

```{python}
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_smooth, facet_wrap, labs, theme_bw

p = (ggplot(penguins, aes("flipper_length_mm", "body_mass_g", color="species"))
     + geom_point(alpha=0.7)
     + geom_smooth(method="lm", se=False)
     + facet_wrap("~sex")
     + labs(x="Flipper length (mm)", y="Body mass (g)", title="plotnine")
     + theme_bw())
p.draw(show=True)
```

## pandas

```{python}
ax = penguins.pivot_table(index="species", columns="sex", values="body_mass_g").plot.bar(rot=0)
ax.set_ylabel("Mean body mass (g)")
plt.show()
```

## statsmodels: a linear model and its diagnostics

```{python}
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

model = smf.ols("body_mass_g ~ flipper_length_mm + C(species)", data=penguins).fit()
print(model.summary().tables[1])
```

```{python}
import statsmodels.api as sm

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
axes[0].scatter(model.fittedvalues, model.resid, s=10)
axes[0].axhline(0, color="gray")
axes[0].set(xlabel="Fitted", ylabel="Residual", title="Residuals")
sm.qqplot(model.resid, line="45", fit=True, ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title("Q-Q plot")
fig.tight_layout()
```
